newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Dayton estimates raised.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Dayton estimates raised.

text.p: -- Piper Jaffray analyst Saul Yaari said Thursday he raised his estimates for Dayton Hudson Corp's earnings for 1996 and 1997.
-- Yaari lifted his estimate for the 1996 third quarter to $0.40 a share from $0.34 previously, and he increased his fourth-quarter estimate to $1.29 from $1.23.
-- For the full year, Yaari raised his estimate to $2.27 from $2.15. This compares with $1.29 last year.
-- For 1997, the analyst expects Dayton Hudson will earn $2.50 versus his previous estimate of $2.42.

-- Sales at Dayton Hudson were stronger than expected during October, Yaari said. He now estimates the retailer will post a gain of four percent in same-store sales for October versus his previous estimate a 1.3 percent gain.
-- At Target, same-store sales rose by an estimated eight percent, rebounding from a disappointing 0.9 percent increase in September, Yaari said.
-- Dayton Hudson will cut costs by $170 million this year, Yaari said. The sale of more expensive goods at its department stores and an overhaul of merchandise at Mervyn's also have boosted profits.
